groups.sentence: Instructors choose and use approved or university-licensed AI tools, checking the approved list first.
Users check with IT or get a review before adopting, purchasing or adding AI tools that are not approved.
Instructors do not require students to create accounts with non-university AI tools that collect personal information.
Instructors encourage students to use university-approved AI tools and tell them where to find them.
Students use university-approved or provided AI tools, signed in with their university account, for academic work.
Everyone uses only university-approved or licensed AI tools, logged in with their university account.
Sensitive, non-public or institutional data is used only in approved AI tools.
Employees and staff use only approved or licensed AI tools when working with university data or business.
Instructors use only approved AI tools, including when assessing student work.
Approved tools are vetted and come with data protection and security safeguards that other tools may lack.
The university provides, licenses or gives access to specific AI tools for its community.
Approved or licensed AI tools may be used within the data limits set for each tool.
A list of approved AI tools is published on university web pages or through IT.
Users do not use unapproved, personal or third-party AI tools or accounts for university work.
The university maintains and communicates the list of approved AI tools.
Only university-approved AI meeting and transcription tools are used; unapproved third-party bots are not permitted.
